verdict.rationale: Pipedream MCP is built for acting on behalf of each of your users. Each request carries an x-pd-external-user-id header, and the proxy attaches that connected user's credentials, with managed token storage and refresh and user-revocable access. That covers the core per-user connected-account model. The documented Bearer token, however, sits alongside project-level headers, and nothing shows tokens scoped per end user or states an isolation guarantee between users. missing for 10: documented per-end-user scoped tokens, explicit cross-user isolation guarantee, independent/hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can maintain separate connected accounts and scoped tokens per end user of my product, so each user's agent acts only on that user's credentials

citations.quote: Add Pipedream MCP to your app or agent to make tool calls on behalf of your users to 3,000+ APIs and 10,000+ tools.
the proxy forwards your request with the connected user's credentials attached.
you don’t need to build any authorization flows or deal with token storage and refresh
Users can revoke access to their connected accounts at any time
never directly exposing credentials to AI models
